candidate.educational_objective: Apply current authoritative guidance to identify the uniquely safest or most accurate nursing response for the clinical construct tested by V2-Q0195.

options.A: Use the pump's programmed rate as the sole indicator of tolerance because subjective symptoms, abdominal findings, and stool or flatus patterns do not reliably affect feeding decisions.
options.B: Automatically stop all enteral nutrition whenever any measurable gastric residual is obtained, even when the client has no other evidence of feeding intolerance.
options.C: Rely only on the presence of bowel sounds because bowel sounds are the most accurate single measure of aspiration risk and gastric emptying in enterally fed clients.
options.D: Assess the client's symptoms and abdominal findings and follow the facility's evidence-based protocol; do not rely on a single gastric residual value as the sole tolerance measure.

candidate.rationale: ASPEN recommends evaluating enteral-feeding tolerance using multiple clinical parameters such as nausea, vomiting, abdominal distention, pain, stool/flatus patterns, physical findings, and the overall clinical course. Gastric residual volume should not be used as a stand-alone determinant of tolerance, and routine GRV monitoring may not be necessary in some settings.
